title: Bancorp Collapse Exposes Systemic Banking Fragility
reason: Multiple independent sources confirm this materially as described. IPS Noticias (contemporaneous Oct 1999 wire report) confirms: Central Bank forced liquidation of Banco Corporativo (Bancorp) announced October 7, 1999; cause was overdrafted fiduciary/trust accounts (~$68.9M) with attractive rates but no real backing; Bancorp was only the second bank failure in Honduras in 18 years; five other credit institutions were reported to be in similar trouble; Congress had approved a Financial Stabilization Law the week prior, creating a deposit guarantee fund. El Pulso's investigative series (independent Honduran outlet, 2017/2020) confirms the crisis widened 1998-2003 to include Banco Hondureño de Créditos y Servicios (BAHNCRESER/BANCRESER) and Banco Capital (which collapsed in 2002), and states verbatim: 'Sólo en la liquidación de BANCORP y CAPITAL, el Estado de Honduras extendió fideicomisos por un monto de por lo menos 1,600 millones de lempiras (900 para BANCORP y 580 para CAPITAL) para pagar cuentas de ahorro y cheques a unos 90 mil cuentahabientes (50 mil de BANCORP y 40 mil de CAPITAL)' — an almost exact match to the event's '1,600 million lempiras in guarantees to roughly 90,000 depositors.' Government awareness since 1998 is corroborated by El Pulso noting Bancorp's problems emerged in late 1998 before the 1999 forced liquidation. All material details (date, mechanism, scope, aftermath, figures) check out against independent contemporaneous and investigative reporting.
